Tutorial 4 — Climate Stress-Test Experiment

Hurricane Wind Hazard Model for the Caribbean

2026-04-16

Source: vignettes/tutorial_4_stress_test.qmd

Prerequisites

This tutorial builds on Tutorial 3. You should already be familiar with make_hazard_cfg(), run_hazard_model(), and named KNMI’23 climate scenarios.

This tutorial shows how to design a climate stress-test experiment: pick a handful of high-impact synthetic years from a long stationary baseline, then replay those same years under future-climate scenarios using common random numbers (CRN). The result is a directly comparable set of daily wind traces where any difference between baseline and future is attributable to climate forcing alone.

1 What This Tutorial Covers

By the end, you will be able to:

  • generate a long stationary baseline and rate years on a composite stress score
  • pick representative high-impact years at fixed severity quantiles (Q50–Q99)
  • replay those year indices under KNMI’23 scenarios with CRN, pinning the dominant event
  • visualize baseline-vs-scenario daily wind traces in a single faceted panel
library(ipdcstorm)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

2 Experiment Configuration

A small block of switches controls the entire experiment. The defaults below run quickly for the vignette; for a production stress-test, raise n_sim to 2,000 or more.

seed            <- 42L
n_sim           <- 500L                       # raise to 2000+ in production
irma_wind_kt    <- 80                         # IRMA-like site-level threshold (kt)
quantile_probs  <- c(0.50, 0.80, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99)
knmi_scenarios  <- c("knmi_Ld", "knmi_Hd")    # low-dry and high-dry KNMI'23
target_year     <- 2100                       # 2050 (near-term) or 2100 (end-of-century)

# Composite rating weights (must sum to 1)
w_peak   <- 0.5   # severity (max site-level peak wind)
w_damage <- 0.5   # accumulation (integrated portfolio damage)

targets <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name,         ~lat,     ~lon,
  "St_Martin",   18.0708, -63.0501,
  "Saba",        17.6350, -63.2300,
  "Statia",      17.4890, -62.9740,
  "Puerto_Rico", 18.4655, -66.1057,
  "Miami",       25.7617, -80.1918
)

ibtracs_demo <- system.file("extdata", "ibtracs_demo.csv", package = "ipdcstorm")

3 Part 1 — Baseline & Year Selection

We first run a stationary baseline of n_sim synthetic years and downscale every year to daily wind and damage at every target location.

cfg_base <- make_hazard_cfg(
  data_path        = ibtracs_demo,
  simulation_years = n_sim,
  climate          = make_climate_cfg(scenario = "stationary")
)

out_base <- run_hazard_model(cfg_base, targets = targets, seed = seed, verbose = FALSE)

daily_base_list <- generate_daily_hazard_impact_spatial(
  out         = out_base,
  location    = targets$name,
  sim_years   = seq_len(n_sim),
  year0       = 2000L,
  gust_factor = 1.0,
  damage      = list(method = "intensity"),
  pulse_shape = "cosine",
  scenario    = "baseline",
  seed        = seed
)

Including trade-wind background in stress tests

Pass a make_background_wind_cfg() object to make_hazard_cfg() to fill non-storm days with realistic wind speeds across all stress-test replays. Because it is stored in cfg, it is embedded in every out object and picked up automatically by each generate_daily_hazard_impact_spatial() call — both the baseline above and all scenario replays below — with no extra arguments required. This keeps the CRN isolation intact: the background wind is generated with seed + 1, so the storm-sampling RNG is unaffected. See Tutorial 1 §Background Wind for a full example.

3.1 Annual metrics across all sites

Each year is summarised on basin-wide metrics: peak site-level wind, hurricane- and storm-day counts, and integrated damage across all sites.

daily_base <- bind_rows(daily_base_list)

annual_all <- daily_base |>
  group_by(sim_year, location) |>
  summarise(
    peak_wind_kt = max(wind_kt, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_hur_days   = sum(wind_kt >= 64, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_storm_days = sum(wind_kt >= 34, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_damage = sum(damage_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(sim_year) |>
  summarise(
    peak_wind_max    = max(peak_wind_kt),
    hur_days_total   = sum(n_hur_days),
    storm_days_total = sum(n_storm_days),
    damage_total     = sum(total_damage),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

3.2 Composite stress rating

Candidate years must contain at least one IRMA-class event (peak wind ≥ 80 kt). Surviving years are rank-normalised on two metrics and combined into a single rating in [0, 1]:

Metric Meaning
r_peak Worst single-site peak wind (severity; loss scales ~wind³).
r_damage Sum of damage_rate across days and sites (integrated impact). 
irma_candidates <- annual_all |>
  filter(peak_wind_max >= irma_wind_kt)

n_cand <- nrow(irma_candidates)

irma_rated <- irma_candidates |>
  mutate(
    r_peak   = rank(peak_wind_max, ties.method = "average") / n_cand,
    r_damage = rank(damage_total,  ties.method = "average") / n_cand,
    rating   = w_peak * r_peak + w_damage * r_damage
  ) |>
  arrange(rating)

# Pick years at the target quantiles of the rating distribution
sel_pos      <- pmax(1L, ceiling(quantile_probs * n_cand))
selected_ids <- irma_rated$sim_year[sel_pos]

irma_rated |>
  filter(sim_year %in% selected_ids) |>
  mutate(
    quantile = paste0("Q", round(quantile_probs * 100), "%")
  ) |>
  select(quantile, sim_year, peak_wind_max, hur_days_total,
         damage_total, rating)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   quantile sim_year peak_wind_max hur_days_total damage_total rating
#>   <chr>       <int>         <dbl>          <int>        <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 Q50%           98         100.0              6       0.0313  0.444
#> 2 Q80%          444         116.              12       0.0924  0.770
#> 3 Q90%           80         150.              11       0.0735  0.893
#> 4 Q95%          257         150.              16       0.0775  0.920
#> 5 Q99%          332         150.              14       0.120   0.950

3.3 Pin the focal event

For each selected year we identify the SID of the basin-level peak hurricane day. Pinning this SID into every scenario run guarantees the focal event always appears, with its intensity and duration perturbed by the scenario’s delta_sst — all other storm slots remain free to vary with climate.

baseline_stress <- lapply(daily_base_list, function(df) {
  df[df$sim_year %in% selected_ids, ]
})

focal_sids <- setNames(vector("list", length(selected_ids)),
                       as.character(selected_ids))

for (yr in selected_ids) {
  yr_hur <- bind_rows(lapply(baseline_stress, function(df) {
    df[df$sim_year == yr & !is.na(df$event_class) & df$event_class == "HUR", ]
  }))
  if (nrow(yr_hur) == 0L) {
    focal_sids[[as.character(yr)]] <- NA_character_
    next
  }
  peak_row <- yr_hur[which.max(yr_hur$wind_kt), ]
  focal_sids[[as.character(yr)]] <- sub("_y[0-9]+_[0-9]+$", "",
                                        peak_row$event_id[1L])
}

focal_sids
#> $`98`
#> [1] "1998259N10335"
#> 
#> $`444`
#> [1] "1999318N17278"
#> 
#> $`80`
#> [1] "2017242N16333"
#> 
#> $`257`
#> [1] "2017242N16333"
#> 
#> $`332`
#> [1] "2017242N16333"

4 Part 2 — KNMI’23 Climate Replays

The same seed and the same sim_years = 1:n_sim vector are used for every scenario. This is the common random numbers trick: the RNG is consumed at exactly the same rate in every run, so year i in the baseline corresponds to year i in the scenario. Differences between traces therefore isolate climate forcing rather than sampling noise.

Why iterate the full 1:n_sim?

Passing only selected_ids to the scenario run would put its first iteration at the initial RNG state, while the baseline reached those same indices after consuming hundreds of prior draws. The result would be completely different event sampling — unrelated to climate.

cc_stress <- vector("list", length(knmi_scenarios))
names(cc_stress) <- knmi_scenarios

for (scen in knmi_scenarios) {
  cfg_cc <- make_hazard_cfg(
    data_path        = ibtracs_demo,
    simulation_years = n_sim,
    climate          = make_climate_cfg(scenario   = scen,
                                        target_year = target_year,
                                        perturb     = TRUE)
  )

  out_cc <- run_hazard_model(cfg_cc, targets = targets,
                             seed = seed, verbose = FALSE)

  cc_daily_all <- generate_daily_hazard_impact_spatial(
    out         = out_cc,
    location    = targets$name,
    sim_years   = seq_len(n_sim),
    year0       = 2000L,
    gust_factor = 1.0,
    damage      = list(method = "intensity"),
    pulse_shape = "cosine",
    scenario    = scen,
    seed        = seed,
    pinned_sids = focal_sids
  )

  cc_stress[[scen]] <- lapply(cc_daily_all, function(df) {
    df[df$sim_year %in% selected_ids, ]
  })
}

5 Part 3 — Visualize the Stress-Test Traces

Each panel below is one selected year, with the stationary baseline (black) overlaid against the KNMI’23 scenarios (blue = low-dry, red = high-dry). Reference dashes mark the tropical-storm (34 kt) and hurricane (64 kt) thresholds.

focal_location <- "Saba"

scenario_labels <- c(
  "Baseline" = "Baseline (stationary)",
  "knmi_Ld"  = "KNMI L-d (low warming, dry)",
  "knmi_Hd"  = "KNMI H-d (high warming, dry)"
)
scenario_colors <- c(
  "Baseline" = "black",
  "knmi_Ld"  = "#4575b4",
  "knmi_Hd"  = "#d73027"
)

# Hurricane season window (Jun 1 – Dec 31, non-leap)
season_doy_start <- 152L
season_doy_end   <- 365L
month_doy_all    <- cumsum(c(1L, 31L, 28L, 31L, 30L, 31L,
                             30L, 31L, 31L, 30L, 31L, 30L))
season_months    <- 6:12
month_doy_starts <- month_doy_all[season_months]
month_labels     <- month.abb[season_months]

base_df <- baseline_stress[[focal_location]] |>
  mutate(scenario = "Baseline",
         doy      = as.integer(format(date, "%j")))

knmi_df <- bind_rows(lapply(knmi_scenarios, function(scen) {
  cc_stress[[scen]][[focal_location]] |>
    mutate(scenario = scen,
           doy      = as.integer(format(date, "%j")))
}))

trace_labels <- setNames(
  paste0("Trace ", seq_along(selected_ids),
         "  \u2014  Q", round(quantile_probs * 100), "%"),
  as.character(selected_ids)
)

plot_df <- bind_rows(knmi_df, base_df) |>
  filter(doy >= season_doy_start, doy <= season_doy_end) |>
  mutate(
    scenario    = factor(scenario, levels = c(knmi_scenarios, "Baseline")),
    trace_label = factor(trace_labels[as.character(sim_year)],
                         levels = trace_labels)
  )
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = doy, y = wind_kt)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 34, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "#E69F00", linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 64, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "#d73027", linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = ~ filter(.x, scenario != "Baseline"),
            aes(colour = scenario), linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_line(data = ~ filter(.x, scenario == "Baseline"),
            aes(colour = scenario), linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = scenario_colors,
                      labels = scenario_labels,
                      breaks = c("Baseline", knmi_scenarios),
                      name   = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(season_doy_start, season_doy_end),
                     breaks = month_doy_starts,
                     labels = month_labels,
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  facet_wrap(~ trace_label, nrow = 5, ncol = 1, scales = "fixed") +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Sustained wind speed (kt)",
    title = sprintf("%s \u2014 Stress-test wind traces: baseline vs KNMI\u201923",
                    focal_location),
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "%d high-impact years from %d synthetic years (seed = %d, target year %d)",
      length(selected_ids), n_sim, seed, target_year),
    caption = "Dashed: TS (34 kt, orange) and hurricane (64 kt, red) thresholds"
  ) +
  theme_light(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    legend.key.width = unit(1.4, "cm"),
    strip.text       = element_text(size = 8.5, face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing.y  = unit(0.4, "lines"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey40"),
    plot.caption     = element_text(size = 7, colour = "grey50", hjust = 0)
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1,
                               override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.1)))

6 Where to Go Next

  • Switch target_year to 2050 to compare near-term vs end-of-century forcing.
  • Add knmi_Ln / knmi_Hn to knmi_scenarios for the wet variants.
  • Tune w_peak / w_damage to bias year selection toward severity vs accumulation.
  • Change focal_location to view the same experiment from a different island.
  • For a production run, point data_path at the full IBTrACS NA CSV and raise n_sim to ≥ 2,000.
